        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### Two Authoritative Design Decisions to Keep in Mind\n\n**1. DragCoordinator is the central abstraction.** The user explicitly asked for it. Both drag adapters (useClipDrag for pointer drag, useExternalDrop for HTML5 drag) call `coordinator.update()` and `coordinator.end()`. Neither adapter touches the indicator directly or computes screen positions \u2014 the coordinator does that via `computeDropPosition` (from `drop-position.ts`). Adapters read `coordinator.lastPosition` when they need to know where to drop.\n\n**2. The coordinator lives at provider level, not component level.** `useDragCoordinator` is called in `useTimelineState` (which runs in `VideoEditorProvider`). It creates `indicatorRef` and `editAreaRef` and exposes them in context. `TimelineEditor.tsx` is a consumer \u2014 it reads the refs from context, wires `<DropIndicator ref={indicatorRef}>` into the DOM, and captures the editArea element into `editAreaRef`. This resolves the context-inversion flag from the previous iteration and is the correct architecture given that `useExternalDrop` (also called in `useTimelineState`) needs the coordinator.\n\n### Open Flag Resolution\n\nThe only unresolved flag (drag-coordinator-phase3-stale-extraction) is a copy-paste artifact in the plan text. Phase 3 Step 8 still says `useExternalDrop` should take `indicatorRef` as an arg and contain `getDropPosition`/`getTimelineDomNodes` \u2014 that's stale from v1. The authoritative design is Phase 2: `useExternalDrop` takes `coordinator` as an arg, position math is in `drop-position.ts` via the coordinator. Tasks T9/T11 in this briefing reflect the corrected design.\n\n### Phase Dependencies and Parallelism\n\n- **T1-T3** (Phase 1) are strictly sequential \u2014 each removes code the next depends on.\n- **T4 and T5** (infrastructure) are independent of Phase 1 and of each other \u2014 can be built in parallel with T1-T3.\n- **T6** needs both T4 and T5 complete.\n- **T7** needs T6 (coordinator exists) and T3 (context is clean).\n- **T8 and T9** are independent of each other (different drag systems) but both need T7.\n- **T10-T13** (god hook split) are strictly sequential extractions.\n- **T14** wires everything and needs both T8 and T13.\n\n### Extraction Strategy for Phase 3\n\nExtract in dependency order: useAssetManagement first (T10, pure data, no DOM), then useExternalDrop (T11, depends on asset management exports), then useClipResize (T12, clean independent boundary), then rename what's left to useClipEditing (T13). Each step should leave TypeScript compiling \u2014 don't batch extractions.\n\n### The Library Relationship After This Work\n\nAfter T1, `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` serves exactly 4 purposes: (1) time-scale rendering, (2) virtualized grid layout, (3) cursor/playhead, (4) action resize via interact.js + `flexible:true`. It no longer owns drag. `onChange` becomes resize-only sync. `onActionResize*` callbacks remain wired through useClipResize.\n\n### What NOT to Touch\n\n- The floating ghost clone in useClipDrag (imperative DOM clone, SETTLED-004)\n- Library resize functionality (flexible:true preserved, onActionResize* stay wired)\n- Any code outside `src/tools/video-editor/` (this refactor is entirely self-contained)\n- The RAF throttle pattern (still needed for dragover coalescing, now inside coordinator)"

> DEVELOPER

Execute the approved plan in the repository.

        Project directory:
        /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app

        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

Interface:\n   ```tsx\n   interface DragCoordinator {\n     update(params: {\n       clientX: number;\n       clientY: number;\n       sourceKind: TrackKind | null;\n       clipDuration?: number;\n     }): DropPosition;\n     end(): void;\n     lastPosition: DropPosition | null;\n   }\n   ```\n3. Uses RAF coalescing so rapid updates don't cause 60fps React re-renders.\n5. `end()`: calls `indicatorRef.current?.hide()`, clears `lastPosition`.\n6. Return: `{ coordinator, indicatorRef, editAreaRef }` \u2014 refs exposed so `TimelineEditor` can wire `<DropIndicator ref={indicatorRef}>` and capture the editArea DOM element.\n\n**CRITICAL**: This hook must be called in `useTimelineState` (which runs in VideoEditorProvider, ABOVE TimelineEditor).   "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### Two Authoritative Design Decisions to Keep in Mind\n\n**1. DragCoordinator is the central abstraction.** The user explicitly asked for it. Both drag adapters (useClipDrag for pointer drag, useExternalDrop for HTML5 drag) call `coordinator.update()` and `coordinator.end()`. Neither adapter touches the indicator directly or computes screen positions \u2014 the coordinator does that via `computeDropPosition` (from `drop-position.ts`). Adapters read `coordinator.lastPosition` when they need to know where to drop.\n\n**2. The coordinator lives at provider level, not component level.** `useDragCoordinator` is called in `useTimelineState` (which runs in `VideoEditorProvider`). It creates `indicatorRef` and `editAreaRef` and exposes them in context. `TimelineEditor.tsx` is a consumer \u2014 it reads the refs from context, wires `<DropIndicator ref={indicatorRef}>` into the DOM, and captures the editArea element into `editAreaRef`. This resolves the context-inversion flag from the previous iteration and is the correct architecture given that `useExternalDrop` (also called in `useTimelineState`) needs the coordinator.\n\n### Open Flag Resolution\n\nThe only unresolved flag (drag-coordinator-phase3-stale-extraction) is a copy-paste artifact in the plan text. Phase 3 Step 8 still says `useExternalDrop` should take `indicatorRef` as an arg and contain `getDropPosition`/`getTimelineDomNodes` \u2014 that's stale from v1. The authoritative design is Phase 2: `useExternalDrop` takes `coordinator` as an arg, position math is in `drop-position.ts` via the coordinator. Tasks T9/T11 in this briefing reflect the corrected design.\n\n### Phase Dependencies and Parallelism\n\n- **T1-T3** (Phase 1) are strictly sequential \u2014 each removes code the next depends on.\n- **T4 and T5** (infrastructure) are independent of Phase 1 and of each other \u2014 can be built in parallel with T1-T3.\n- **T6** needs both T4 and T5 complete.\n- **T7** needs T6 (coordinator exists) and T3 (context is clean).\n- **T8 and T9** are independent of each other (different drag systems) but both need T7.\n- **T10-T13** (god hook split) are strictly sequential extractions.\n- **T14** wires everything and needs both T8 and T13.\n\n### Extraction Strategy for Phase 3\n\nExtract in dependency order: useAssetManagement first (T10, pure data, no DOM), then useExternalDrop (T11, depends on asset management exports), then useClipResize (T12, clean independent boundary), then rename what's left to useClipEditing (T13). Each step should leave TypeScript compiling \u2014 don't batch extractions.\n\n### The Library Relationship After This Work\n\nAfter T1, `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` serves exactly 4 purposes: (1) time-scale rendering, (2) virtualized grid layout, (3) cursor/playhead, (4) action resize via interact.js + `flexible:true`. It no longer owns drag. `onChange` becomes resize-only sync. `onActionResize*` callbacks remain wired through useClipResize.\n\n### What NOT to Touch\n\n- The floating ghost clone in useClipDrag (imperative DOM clone, SETTLED-004)\n- Library resize functionality (flexible:true preserved, onActionResize* stay wired)\n- Any code outside `src/tools/video-editor/` (this refactor is entirely self-contained)\n- The RAF throttle pattern (still needed for dragover coalescing, now inside coordinator)"

        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### Two Authoritative Design Decisions to Keep in Mind\n\n**1. DragCoordinator is the central abstraction.** The user explicitly asked for it. Both drag adapters (useClipDrag for pointer drag, useExternalDrop for HTML5 drag) call `coordinator.update()` and `coordinator.end()`. Neither adapter touches the indicator directly or computes screen positions \u2014 the coordinator does that via `computeDropPosition` (from `drop-position.ts`). Adapters read `coordinator.lastPosition` when they need to know where to drop.\n\n**2. The coordinator lives at provider level, not component level.** `useDragCoordinator` is called in `useTimelineState` (which runs in `VideoEditorProvider`). It creates `indicatorRef` and `editAreaRef` and exposes them in context. `TimelineEditor.tsx` is a consumer \u2014 it reads the refs from context, wires `<DropIndicator ref={indicatorRef}>` into the DOM, and captures the editArea element into `editAreaRef`. This resolves the context-inversion flag from the previous iteration and is the correct architecture given that `useExternalDrop` (also called in `useTimelineState`) needs the coordinator.\n\n### Open Flag Resolution\n\nThe only unresolved flag (drag-coordinator-phase3-stale-extraction) is a copy-paste artifact in the plan text. Phase 3 Step 8 still says `useExternalDrop` should take `indicatorRef` as an arg and contain `getDropPosition`/`getTimelineDomNodes` \u2014 that's stale from v1. The authoritative design is Phase 2: `useExternalDrop` takes `coordinator` as an arg, position math is in `drop-position.ts` via the coordinator. Tasks T9/T11 in this briefing reflect the corrected design.\n\n### Phase Dependencies and Parallelism\n\n- **T1-T3** (Phase 1) are strictly sequential \u2014 each removes code the next depends on.\n- **T4 and T5** (infrastructure) are independent of Phase 1 and of each other \u2014 can be built in parallel with T1-T3.\n- **T6** needs both T4 and T5 complete.\n- **T7** needs T6 (coordinator exists) and T3 (context is clean).\n- **T8 and T9** are independent of each other (different drag systems) but both need T7.\n- **T10-T13** (god hook split) are strictly sequential extractions.\n- **T14** wires everything and needs both T8 and T13.\n\n### Extraction Strategy for Phase 3\n\nExtract in dependency order: useAssetManagement first (T10, pure data, no DOM), then useExternalDrop (T11, depends on asset management exports), then useClipResize (T12, clean independent boundary), then rename what's left to useClipEditing (T13). Each step should leave TypeScript compiling \u2014 don't batch extractions.\n\n### The Library Relationship After This Work\n\nAfter T1, `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` serves exactly 4 purposes: (1) time-scale rendering, (2) virtualized grid layout, (3) cursor/playhead, (4) action resize via interact.js + `flexible:true`. It no longer owns drag. `onChange` becomes resize-only sync. `onActionResize*` callbacks remain wired through useClipResize.\n\n### What NOT to Touch\n\n- The floating ghost clone in useClipDrag (imperative DOM clone, SETTLED-004)\n- Library resize functionality (flexible:true preserved, onActionResize* stay wired)\n- Any code outside `src/tools/video-editor/` (this refactor is entirely self-contained)\n- The RAF throttle pattern (still needed for dragover coalescing, now inside coordinator)"

> DEVELOPER

Execute the approved plan in the repository.

        Project directory:
        /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app

        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

Adapters read `coordinator.lastPosition` when they need to know where to drop.\n\n**2. This resolves the context-inversion flag from the previous iteration and is the correct architecture given that `useExternalDrop` (also called in `useTimelineState`) needs the coordinator.\n\n### Open Flag Resolution\n\nThe only unresolved flag (drag-coordinator-phase3-stale-extraction) is a copy-paste artifact in the plan text. The authoritative design is Phase 2: `useExternalDrop` takes `coordinator` as an arg, position math is in `drop-position.ts` via the coordinator.         Project directory:

        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

Neither adapter touches the indicator directly or computes screen positions \u2014 the coordinator does that via `computeDropPosition` (from `drop-position.ts`). Adapters read `coordinator.lastPosition` when they need to know where to drop.\n\n**2. This resolves the context-inversion flag from the previous iteration and is the correct architecture given that `useExternalDrop` (also called in `useTimelineState`) needs the coordinator.\n\n### Open Flag Resolution\n\nThe only unresolved flag (drag-coordinator-phase3-stale-extraction) is a copy-paste artifact in the plan text. > DEVELOPER

Execute the approved plan in the repository.

        Project directory:
        /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app

        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### Two Authoritative Design Decisions to Keep in Mind\n\n**1. DragCoordinator is the central abstraction.** The user explicitly asked for it. Both drag adapters (useClipDrag for pointer drag, useExternalDrop for HTML5 drag) call `coordinator.update()` and `coordinator.end()`. Neither adapter touches the indicator directly or computes screen positions \u2014 the coordinator does that via `computeDropPosition` (from `drop-position.ts`). Adapters read `coordinator.lastPosition` when they need to know where to drop.\n\n**2. The coordinator lives at provider level, not component level.** `useDragCoordinator` is called in `useTimelineState` (which runs in `VideoEditorProvider`). It creates `indicatorRef` and `editAreaRef` and exposes them in context. `TimelineEditor.tsx` is a consumer \u2014 it reads the refs from context, wires `<DropIndicator ref={indicatorRef}>` into the DOM, and captures the editArea element into `editAreaRef`. This resolves the context-inversion flag from the previous iteration and is the correct architecture given that `useExternalDrop` (also called in `useTimelineState`) needs the coordinator.\n\n### Open Flag Resolution\n\nThe only unresolved flag (drag-coordinator-phase3-stale-extraction) is a copy-paste artifact in the plan text. Phase 3 Step 8 still says `useExternalDrop` should take `indicatorRef` as an arg and contain `getDropPosition`/`getTimelineDomNodes` \u2014 that's stale from v1. The authoritative design is Phase 2: `useExternalDrop` takes `coordinator` as an arg, position math is in `drop-position.ts` via the coordinator. Tasks T9/T11 in this briefing reflect the corrected design.\n\n### Phase Dependencies and Parallelism\n\n- **T1-T3** (Phase 1) are strictly sequential \u2014 each removes code the next depends on.\n- **T4 and T5** (infrastructure) are independent of Phase 1 and of each other \u2014 can be built in parallel with T1-T3.\n- **T6** needs both T4 and T5 complete.\n- **T7** needs T6 (coordinator exists) and T3 (context is clean).\n- **T8 and T9** are independent of each other (different drag systems) but both need T7.\n- **T10-T13** (god hook split) are strictly sequential extractions.\n- **T14** wires everything and needs both T8 and T13.\n\n### Extraction Strategy for Phase 3\n\nExtract in dependency order: useAssetManagement first (T10, pure data, no DOM), then useExternalDrop (T11, depends on asset management exports), then useClipResize (T12, clean independent boundary), then rename what's left to useClipEditing (T13). Each step should leave TypeScript compiling \u2014 don't batch extractions.\n\n### The Library Relationship After This Work\n\nAfter T1, `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` serves exactly 4 purposes: (1) time-scale rendering, (2) virtualized grid layout, (3) cursor/playhead, (4) action resize via interact.js + `flexible:true`. It no longer owns drag. `onChange` becomes resize-only sync. `onActionResize*` callbacks remain wired through useClipResize.\n\n### What NOT to Touch\n\n- The floating ghost clone in useClipDrag (imperative DOM clone, SETTLED-004)\n- Library resize functionality (flexible:true preserved, onActionResize* stay wired)\n- Any code outside `src/tools/video-editor/` (this refactor is entirely self-contained)\n- The RAF throttle pattern (still needed for dragover coalescing, now inside coordinator)"

> DEVELOPER

Execute the approved plan in the repository.

        Project directory:
        /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app

        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### Two Authoritative Design Decisions to Keep in Mind\n\n**1. DragCoordinator is the central abstraction.** The user explicitly asked for it. Both drag adapters (useClipDrag for pointer drag, useExternalDrop for HTML5 drag) call `coordinator.update()` and `coordinator.end()`. Neither adapter touches the indicator directly or computes screen positions \u2014 the coordinator does that via `computeDropPosition` (from `drop-position.ts`). Adapters read `coordinator.lastPosition` when they need to know where to drop.\n\n**2. The coordinator lives at provider level, not component level.** `useDragCoordinator` is called in `useTimelineState` (which runs in `VideoEditorProvider`). It creates `indicatorRef` and `editAreaRef` and exposes them in context. `TimelineEditor.tsx` is a consumer \u2014 it reads the refs from context, wires `<DropIndicator ref={indicatorRef}>` into the DOM, and captures the editArea element into `editAreaRef`. This resolves the context-inversion flag from the previous iteration and is the correct architecture given that `useExternalDrop` (also called in `useTimelineState`) needs the coordinator.\n\n### Open Flag Resolution\n\nThe only unresolved flag (drag-coordinator-phase3-stale-extraction) is a copy-paste artifact in the plan text. Phase 3 Step 8 still says `useExternalDrop` should take `indicatorRef` as an arg and contain `getDropPosition`/`getTimelineDomNodes` \u2014 that's stale from v1. The authoritative design is Phase 2: `useExternalDrop` takes `coordinator` as an arg, position math is in `drop-position.ts` via the coordinator. Tasks T9/T11 in this briefing reflect the corrected design.\n\n### Phase Dependencies and Parallelism\n\n- **T1-T3** (Phase 1) are strictly sequential \u2014 each removes code the next depends on.\n- **T4 and T5** (infrastructure) are independent of Phase 1 and of each other \u2014 can be built in parallel with T1-T3.\n- **T6** needs both T4 and T5 complete.\n- **T7** needs T6 (coordinator exists) and T3 (context is clean).\n- **T8 and T9** are independent of each other (different drag systems) but both need T7.\n- **T10-T13** (god hook split) are strictly sequential extractions.\n- **T14** wires everything and needs both T8 and T13.\n\n### Extraction Strategy for Phase 3\n\nExtract in dependency order: useAssetManagement first (T10, pure data, no DOM), then useExternalDrop (T11, depends on asset management exports), then useClipResize (T12, clean independent boundary), then rename what's left to useClipEditing (T13). Each step should leave TypeScript compiling \u2014 don't batch extractions.\n\n### The Library Relationship After This Work\n\nAfter T1, `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` serves exactly 4 purposes: (1) time-scale rendering, (2) virtualized grid layout, (3) cursor/playhead, (4) action resize via interact.js + `flexible:true`. It no longer owns drag. `onChange` becomes resize-only sync. `onActionResize*` callbacks remain wired through useClipResize.\n\n### What NOT to Touch\n\n- The floating ghost clone in useClipDrag (imperative DOM clone, SETTLED-004)\n- Library resize functionality (flexible:true preserved, onActionResize* stay wired)\n- Any code outside `src/tools/video-editor/` (this refactor is entirely self-contained)\n- The RAF throttle pattern (still needed for dragover coalescing, now inside coordinator)"

> DEVELOPER

Execute the approved plan in the repository.

        Project directory:
        /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app

        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### Two Authoritative Design Decisions to Keep in Mind\n\n**1. DragCoordinator is the central abstraction.** The user explicitly asked for it. Both drag adapters (useClipDrag for pointer drag, useExternalDrop for HTML5 drag) call `coordinator.update()` and `coordinator.end()`. Neither adapter touches the indicator directly or computes screen positions \u2014 the coordinator does that via `computeDropPosition` (from `drop-position.ts`). Adapters read `coordinator.lastPosition` when they need to know where to drop.\n\n**2. The coordinator lives at provider level, not component level.** `useDragCoordinator` is called in `useTimelineState` (which runs in `VideoEditorProvider`). This resolves the context-inversion flag from the previous iteration and is the correct architecture given that `useExternalDrop` (also called in `useTimelineState`) needs the coordinator.\n\n### Open Flag Resolution\n\nThe only unresolved flag (drag-coordinator-phase3-stale-extraction) is a copy-paste artifact in the plan text. Each step should leave TypeScript compiling \u2014 don't batch extractions.\n\n### The Library Relationship After This Work\n\nAfter T1, `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` serves exactly 4 purposes: (1) time-scale rendering, (2) virtualized grid layout, (3) cursor/playhead, (4) action resize via interact.js + `flexible:true`. It no longer owns drag. `onChange` becomes resize-only sync. `onActionResize*` callbacks remain wired through useClipResize.\n\n### What NOT to Touch\n\n- The floating ghost clone in useClipDrag (imperative DOM clone, SETTLED-004)\n- Library resize functionality (flexible:true preserved, onActionResize* stay wired)\n- Any code outside `src/tools/video-editor/` (this refactor is entirely self-contained)\n- The RAF throttle pattern (still needed for dragover coalescing, now inside coordinator)"

> DEVELOPER

Execute the approved plan in the repository.

        Project directory:
        /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app

        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

Interface:\n   ```tsx\n   interface DragCoordinator {\n     update(params: {\n       clientX: number;\n       clientY: number;\n       sourceKind: TrackKind | null;\n       clipDuration?: number;\n     }): DropPosition;\n     end(): void;\n     lastPosition: DropPosition | null;\n   }\n   ```\n3.   "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### Two Authoritative Design Decisions to Keep in Mind\n\n**1. DragCoordinator is the central abstraction.** The user explicitly asked for it. Both drag adapters (useClipDrag for pointer drag, useExternalDrop for HTML5 drag) call `coordinator.update()` and `coordinator.end()`. Neither adapter touches the indicator directly or computes screen positions \u2014 the coordinator does that via `computeDropPosition` (from `drop-position.ts`). Adapters read `coordinator.lastPosition` when they need to know where to drop.\n\n**2. The coordinator lives at provider level, not component level.** `useDragCoordinator` is called in `useTimelineState` (which runs in `VideoEditorProvider`). It creates `indicatorRef` and `editAreaRef` and exposes them in context. `TimelineEditor.tsx` is a consumer \u2014 it reads the refs from context, wires `<DropIndicator ref={indicatorRef}>` into the DOM, and captures the editArea element into `editAreaRef`. This resolves the context-inversion flag from the previous iteration and is the correct architecture given that `useExternalDrop` (also called in `useTimelineState`) needs the coordinator.\n\n### Open Flag Resolution\n\nThe only unresolved flag (drag-coordinator-phase3-stale-extraction) is a copy-paste artifact in the plan text. Phase 3 Step 8 still says `useExternalDrop` should take `indicatorRef` as an arg and contain `getDropPosition`/`getTimelineDomNodes` \u2014 that's stale from v1. The authoritative design is Phase 2: `useExternalDrop` takes `coordinator` as an arg, position math is in `drop-position.ts` via the coordinator. Tasks T9/T11 in this briefing reflect the corrected design.\n\n### Phase Dependencies and Parallelism\n\n- **T1-T3** (Phase 1) are strictly sequential \u2014 each removes code the next depends on.\n- **T4 and T5** (infrastructure) are independent of Phase 1 and of each other \u2014 can be built in parallel with T1-T3.\n- **T6** needs both T4 and T5 complete.\n- **T7** needs T6 (coordinator exists) and T3 (context is clean).\n- **T8 and T9** are independent of each other (different drag systems) but both need T7.\n- **T10-T13** (god hook split) are strictly sequential extractions.\n- **T14** wires everything and needs both T8 and T13.\n\n### Extraction Strategy for Phase 3\n\nExtract in dependency order: useAssetManagement first (T10, pure data, no DOM), then useExternalDrop (T11, depends on asset management exports), then useClipResize (T12, clean independent boundary), then rename what's left to useClipEditing (T13). Each step should leave TypeScript compiling \u2014 don't batch extractions.\n\n### The Library Relationship After This Work\n\nAfter T1, `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` serves exactly 4 purposes: (1) time-scale rendering, (2) virtualized grid layout, (3) cursor/playhead, (4) action resize via interact.js + `flexible:true`. It no longer owns drag. `onChange` becomes resize-only sync. `onActionResize*` callbacks remain wired through useClipResize.\n\n### What NOT to Touch\n\n- The floating ghost clone in useClipDrag (imperative DOM clone, SETTLED-004)\n- Library resize functionality (flexible:true preserved, onActionResize* stay wired)\n- Any code outside `src/tools/video-editor/` (this refactor is entirely self-contained)\n- The RAF throttle pattern (still needed for dragover coalescing, now inside coordinator)"

        Idea:
Video editor timeline: well-engineered redesign. Core problems: (1) Two competing drag systems (pointer-based useClipDrag + HTML5 useTimelineEditing) each imperatively creating DOM indicator elements — unify into one React-managed indicator system. (2) Timeline library (@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor) is half-used — we capture its pointer events before it sees them, override its move callbacks, but still wire its onActionMove* callbacks through context as dead weight. Either fully own clip movement or fully delegate to the library. (3) Drop indicators are imperative DOM manipulation (createElement, document.body.appendChild) in two places — should be a single React portal component. (4) useTimelineEditing.ts is 947 lines mixing 6 concerns. (5) ActionDragState is a shared mutable ref threaded through 5 files with no coordination. (6) EditorPaneTab has a local height hack that belongs in getEffectivePaneHeights. Goal: a system where there's one clear owner for each concern, indicators are declarative React, the library is either used properly or abstracted away, and the code is obvious to read.

User notes and answers:
- The DragCoordinator should: (1) Accept drag events from two adapters: PointerDragAdapter (wraps useClipDrag's pointer tracking) and Html5DropAdapter (wraps HTML5 dragover/drop). (2) Normalize both into a common DragState: { active, position: DropIndicatorPosition, source: 'clip'|'external', kind: TrackKind|null, isNewTrack, isReject }. (3) Own the DropIndicator ref — adapters call coordinator.update(position), coordinator calls indicatorRef.current.show(). (4) Own cleanup — coordinator.end() hides indicator and resets state. (5) The position computation (row index from Y, time from X, screen coordinates) should be extracted into a shared utility used by both adapters. (6) The floating ghost clone stays in the PointerDragAdapter since it's pointer-specific. (7) Drop handling (what happens on release/drop) stays in the adapters since the actions differ (moveClipToRow vs file upload).

Neither adapter touches the indicator directly or computes screen positions \u2014 the coordinator does that via `computeDropPosition` (from `drop-position.ts`). Adapters read `coordinator.lastPosition` when they need to know where to drop.\n\n**2. The coordinator lives at provider level, not component level.** `useDragCoordinator` is called in `useTimelineState` (which runs in `VideoEditorProvider`). It creates `indicatorRef` and `editAreaRef` and exposes them in context. `TimelineEditor.tsx` is a consumer \u2014 it reads the refs from context, wires `<DropIndicator ref={indicatorRef}>` into the DOM, and captures the editArea element into `editAreaRef`. This resolves the context-inversion flag from the previous iteration and is the correct architecture given that `useExternalDrop` (also called in `useTimelineState`) needs the coordinator.\n\n### Open Flag Resolution\n\nThe only unresolved flag (drag-coordinator-phase3-stale-extraction) is a copy-paste artifact in the plan text. Phase 3 Step 8 still says `useExternalDrop` should take `indicatorRef` as an arg and contain `getDropPosition`/`getTimelineDomNodes` \u2014 that's stale from v1. The authoritative design is Phase 2: `useExternalDrop` takes `coordinator` as an arg, position math is in `drop-position.ts` via the coordinator. Tasks T9/T11 in this briefing reflect the corrected design.\n\n### Phase Dependencies and Parallelism\n\n- **T1-T3** (Phase 1) are strictly sequential \u2014 each removes code the next depends on.\n- **T4 and T5** (infrastructure) are independent of Phase 1 and of each other \u2014 can be built in parallel with T1-T3.\n- **T6** needs both T4 and T5 complete.\n- **T7** needs T6 (coordinator exists) and T3 (context is clean).\n- **T8 and T9** are independent of each other (different drag systems) but both need T7.\n- **T10-T13** (god hook split) are strictly sequential extractions.\n- **T14** wires everything and needs both T8 and T13.\n\n### Extraction Strategy for Phase 3\n\nExtract in dependency order: useAssetManagement first (T10, pure data, no DOM), then useExternalDrop (T11, depends on asset management exports), then useClipResize (T12, clean independent boundary), then rename what's left to useClipEditing (T13). Each step should leave TypeScript compiling \u2014 don't batch extractions.\n\n### The Library Relationship After This Work\n\nAfter T1, `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` serves exactly 4 purposes: (1) time-scale rendering, (2) virtualized grid layout, (3) cursor/playhead, (4) action resize via interact.js + `flexible:true`.
